Date: 2025-01-15
ATTORNEY DOCKET
PATENT APPLICATION
REMARKS
This Application has been carefully reviewed in light of the Office Action mailed October 15, 2024. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of all pending claims in view of the amendments set forth above and the following remarks.
Rejections under 35 U.S.C. # 112
Claims 10, 11, 13-20, 22, 23, and 25-27 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite based on various terms and phrases. Applicant herein amends the claims to address each alleged point of indefiniteness. Accordingly, Applicant requests these rejections be withdrawn.
Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §103
Claims 10, 11, 15-17, 20. 22, 23, and 27 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as being unpatentable over Russell (US 2015/0094618), Drennan (US 2010/0268122), Steiner (WO 2012/114298), and Ten Kate (US 2014/0313030).
Claim 18 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being unpatentable over Russell, Drennan, and Steiner.
Claim 26 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as being unpatentable over Russell, Drennan, Steiner, Ten Kate, and Smith (US 2004/0046668).
Claims 10, 11, 13, 15-17, 19, 20, 22, 23, 25, and 27 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as being unpatentable over Russell, Drennan, Sullivan (US 2007/015603 1), and Ten Kate.
Although Applicant respectfully disagrees, Applicant herein amends independent Claims 10 and 20 to incorporate the features of dependent Claim 14, which is not subject to any prior art based rejections. For example, amended Claim 10 recites the features of:
" decreasing the pressurization measure, at a first depressurization rate, as
a proportional function of a first depressurization period spent on the
support surface but out of the pressurization position;
ATTORNEY DOCKET
PATENT APPLICATION
" detecting the person exiting the support surface and subsequently
returning to the support surface, defining a second depressurization
period spent off the support surface; and
" decreasing the pressurization measure, at a second depressurization rate,
as a proportional function of the second depressurization period spent off
the support surface;
" wherein the second depressurization period is greater than the first
depressurization rate.
Amended Claim 20 recites similar features.
None of the cited references teach or make obvious this combination of features, as confirmed by the absence of rejection of dependent Claim 14. For example, none of the cited references teach the feature of decreasing a pressurization measure at a higher depressurization rate when the patient is detected to be off of the support surface (e.g., out of bed) than when the patient is detected to be on the support surface (e.g., in bed).
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests allowance of amended Claims 10 and 20, along with all pending dependent claims.
Double Patenting Rejections
The Examiner rejected Claims 10, 11, 13-16, 18-20, 22, 23, and 25-27 based on the judicially created double patenting doctrine over Claims 1, 5, 7-9, 1 6, and 18-21 of related U.S. Patent No. 11,051,751 (hereinafter '751 Patent).
Applicants respectfully traverse the rejection. However, to reduce the cost and time required to obtain patent protection, a Terminal Disclaimer filed in compliance with 37 C.F.R. 1.321 is attached hereto, to overcome the double patenting rejection. The '751 patent and the instant patent application are commonly owned by Leaf Healthcare, Inc.
ATTORNEY DOCKET
PATENT APPLICATION
CONCLUSION
Applicant has made an earnest effort to place this case in condition for allowance in light of the remarks set forth above. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the pending claims.
Applicant believes there are no fees due at this time. However, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any fees necessary or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 50-6736 of Slayden Grubert Beard P.L.L.C.
If there are any matters concerning this Application that may be cleared up in a telephone conversation, please contact Applicant's attorney at 512-402-3567.
Respectfully submitted, SLAYDEN GRUBERT BEARD PLLCAttorney for Applicant
